title: Conduct public hearing to update the Austin Strategic Mobility Plan.
summary: Conduct a public hearing and consider an ordinance amending the Imagine Austin Comprehensive Plan to update the Austin Strategic Mobility Plan by adopting the Austin Core Transportation Plan. Funding: This item has no fiscal impact. The public hearing was conducted and a motion to close the public hearing and approve the ordinance was made by Council Member Qadri and seconded by Council Member Velásquez. The following amendment was made by Council Member Qadri and seconded by Council Member Siegel. The amendment was to add the following language to the Austin Core Transportation Plan, page 45: “The conceptual cross sections provided in this plan for the priority projects along 5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th Streets currently depict these streets as largely remaining one- way (with the exception of 7th Street immediately west of I-35, which is recommended for two-way conversion). As these priority projects move forward from planning concepts to preliminary engineering, project staff will evaluate both of these remaining one-way couplets (5th/6th, 7th/8th) and engage the public in identifying opportunities, constraints, impacts, and tradeoffs for potentially converting additional segments of these roadways to two-way operations.

references.quote: While the cross sections presented in this plan will inform starting assumptions for preliminary engineering and design, final preferred cross sections, directionality, modal functions, and transitions will be determined with input from the public during the preliminary engineering process.” The amendment was to also add to pages 7 and 11 under “Major Outcomes” as follows: “Identify Opportunities for Two-Way Conversions: The ACT Plan seeks to reflect this community preference as much as possible by identifying opportunities to convert existing one-way streets to two-way operations while balancing safety, function, and multi-modal needs for downtown.” The amendment was approved on a vote of 10-0.
9-1 — Approved as amended

The public hearing was conducted and a motion to close the public hearing and approve Ordinance No. 20260326-067 for planned unit development (PUD) district zoning, to change conditions of zoning as amended below, was approved on Council Member Fuentes’ motion, Council Member Duchen’s second on a 10-0 vote. Council Member Harper-Madison was off the dais. The staff amendment was to revise Part 4 of the draft ordinance to include the Exhibit “J” – Parking Regulations and Ratio. “GOODNIGHT RANCH PUD PARKING REGULATIONS AND RATIOS ‘EXHIBIT J’ Following are the proposed Goodnight Ranch PUD parking requirements, adapted from the City of Austin Code for Traditional Neighborhood Developments (TND), Section 25-3-83 PARKING (A) The following parking regulations apply within the Goodnight Ranch PUD: (l) There is no off-street loading requirement for a building with less than 10,000 square feet of gross building area. The Director shall determine the location, number, and dimensions of the off-street loading for a larger building. (2) Except as approval by the Director, parking in alleys is prohibited. 24 (3) A parking lot located at the rear or side of a building is preferred and allowed. If a parking lot is located at the front of the building, buffering, in the form of landscaping, henning, decorative walls or fences, is required to buffer pedestrian activity along the street where adjacent to the parking lot. If located at the side of a building, screening shall be provided at, or near, the lot line by landscaping or decorative walls or fences. (4) Compact parking spaces are prohibited. (5) A 25-foot turning radius shall be provided for parking accessed from the alley. (6) Parking spaces are not required for Accessory Dwelling Units. (7) Bicycle parking shall be provided in accordance with Chapter 25-6, Appendix A of the City Code, except as follows: (a) A commercial use parking lot or garage must provide not less than one bicycle parking space for every 10 motor vehicle parking spaces.” The following direction to Staff was as follows: “The City Manager is directed to urgently pursue safety improvements at and near the intersection of Old Lockhart Rd and Slaughter Ln including the installation of a temporary traffic signal. Given the proximity of the City’s corporate limits, improvements should be coordinated in partnership with Travis County. The Goodnight Ranch PUD Transportation Impact Analysis (TIA) Final Memo (C814-04-0187.02.SH) revised January 20, 2022 includes several improvements required of the developer, including the installation of a traffic signal and construction of eastbound and westbound turn lanes as well as a sidewalk on the north side of Slaughter Ln. The City Manager shall continue to pursue these obligations as the development progresses. Any interim safety improvements shall not in any way relieve the developer of their obligations as part of the PUD agreement TIA. The City Manager is directed to report updates to Council on safety improvements within 60 days.” 68. "The City manager is directed to initiate a process to reform the historic tax exemption program to advance equity and align with the historic tax abatement and Transfer of Development Rights recommendations in the Equity Based Historic Preservation Plan. A motion to approve the resolution was made by Council Member Qadri and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Pool. The following amendment was made by Council Member Qadri and seconded by Council Member Vela. The amendment was to add an additional Be It Resolved clause before the existing Be It Resolved clause to read: "The City Manager is directed to return to council with the proposed Equitable Cultural District Funding Model for Council approval by April 2025.

references.quote: Additionally, the City Manager is directed to consider the findings from the funding model and present options for additional funding as needed." The amendment was approved on a 10-0 vote.
10-0 — Approve as amended.

"PART 2. (D) The maximum height of a building or structure on the l roperty fhall not exceed 39.75 feet. (E) An ornamental fence may not be constructed on the northern or southern property lines. A fence constructed on the northern or southern property lines may not be greater than eight feet in height. (F) A 5-foot wide building setback shall be established and maintained along the property lines. Within the building setback, a 3-foot wide vegetative buffer measured from the property lines shall be provided and maintained along property lines. Improvements permitted within the buffer are limited to drainage, underground utility improvements, bio-filtration ponds and components, or those improvements that may otherwise be required by the City of Austin. The public hearing was conducted and a motion to close the public hearing and approve the ordinance was made by Council Member Vela and seconded by Council Member Qadri. The amendment was to revise Part 1 (C) (5) to read: " (5) A screening zone may include: (a) landscaping or gardens; (b) fences, walls, or berms; (c) paths, walkways, or public use trails, including associated lighting and gates; (d) utility infrastructure if a utility provider determines that it is necessary; (e) bike racks, benches, and water fountains; and (f) ground-floor private common and private personal open space. " The amendment was also to revise Part 1 (C) (8) to read: " (8) If existing conditions or proposed utility infrastructure or easements prevent full compliance with the requirements of this section, the director may approve an applicant's request for alternative methods of compliance that aligns with the intent of this section. " l'he amendment was also to revise Part 1 (₺ ) to read: "(F) A compatibility buffer that is at least 10 feet but no more than 15 feet in width must comply with this subsection. (1) The compatibility buffer shall include a screening zone. (2) The screening zone ix parallel to the properly line, begins at the property line, and extends ten feet into the property. 63) At 25 linear feet intervals parallel to the property line that is shared with a triggering property, the screening zone must include a minimum of: (a) two small understory trees; and (b) 10 shrubs. (4) Restricted Zone. The restricted zone is parallel to the property line, begins at the edge of the screening zone, and extends into the property to the maximum width of the compatibility buffer.

title: Amends regulations for land development, including a density bonus program affecting height and compatibility.
summary: Conduct a public hearing and consider an ordinance amending City Code Title 25 (Land Development) to create regulations, including a density bonus program that modifies height and compatibility in exchange for community benefits, for properties that are located within a half mile of the planned Phase 1 Light Rail and Priority Extensions (also known as the Equitable Transit-Oriented Development (ETOD) overlay) The public hearing was conducted and a motion to close the public hearing and approve the ordinance as recommended by staff was made by Council Member Ryan Alter and seconded by AIayor Watson. The following amendment was made by Mayor Pro Tem Pool and seconded by Council Member Vela. The amendment was to revise Section 25-2-654 (E) (2) to read: "(2) Affordability Minimums - Rental Units. If an applicant develops dwelling units for lease, this subdivision applies. (a) To achieve 60 feet or to utilize a development standard under DBETOD that is not height-related, a development must provide a minimum of 10 percent of the residential units as affordable for lease and occupancy by households earning 60 percent or lexx of the current Austin-Round Rock Metropolitan Statistical Area Median Family Income as determined by the director of the Housing Department. (b) To utilize 90 feet in height, a development must provide: (i) a minimum of 12 percent of the residential units as affordable for lease and occupancy by households earning 60 percent or less of the current Austin-Round Rock Metropolitan Statistical Area Median Family Income as determined by the director of the Housing Department; or (ii) a minimum of 10 percent of the residential units as affordable for lease and occupancy by households earning 50 percent or less of the current Austin-Round Rock Metropolitan Statistical Area Median Family. (c) To utilize 120 feet in height, a development must provide: (i) a minimum of 15 percent of the residential units as affordable for leaxe and occupancy by households earning 60 percent or lexx of the current Austin-Round Rock AIetropolitan Statistical Area Median Family Income as determined by the director of the Housing Department; or (ii) a minimum of 12 percent of the residential units as affordable for lease and occupancy by households earning 50 percent or less of the current Austin-Round Rock AIetropolitan Statistical Area AIedian Family" The amendment was also to revise Section 25-2-654 (G) (5) to lead: "(5) Maximum Height.

references.quote: (a) A building may exceed the maximum building height in the base zoning district but no building may exceed 60 feet if the minimum affordability requirements in Subvection (E)(2)(a) are met; or (b) A building may exceed the maximum building height in the base zoning district but no building may exceed 90 feet if the minimum affordability requirements in Subsection (E)(2)(b) are met; or (c) A building may exceed the maximum building height in the base zoning district by 60 feet but no building may exceed 120 feet in height if the minimum affordability requirements in Subsection (10(1) or Subsection CE)(2)(c) are met." The amendment was approved on a 10-1 vote.
10-1 — Approved as amended

The public hearing was conducted and a motion to close the public hearing and approve the ordinance was made by Council Member Alison Alter and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Pool. The amendment was to revise PART 4. 25-9-412 (E) to read: "(E) A development is not required to connect to a reclaimed water line or use reclaimed water when the director of the Housing Department certifies the development is participating in a city, state, or federal program that requires: (1) A minimum of fifty percent on-site income-restricted dwelling units for 60% or lower median family income for rental units; or (2) A minimum of fifty percent on-xite income-re+tricted dwelling units for 80% or lower median family income for ownership units." The amendment was also to revise PART 5. 25-9-414 (B) to read: " (B) A development is not required to have an onsite water reuse system when: (1) the director approves a fee in lieu of providing an onsite water reuse system under Subsection (C); or (2) the director of the liousing Department certifies the development is participating in a city, state, or federal program that requires: (a) a minimum of fifty percent on-site income-restricted dwelling units for 60% or lower median family income for rental units; or (b) a minimum of fifty percent on-site income-restricted dwelling units for 80% or lower median family income for ownership units.

Related to item #70. The public hearing was conducted and a motion to close the public hearing and approve the ordinance was made by Mayor Pro Tem Pool and secon(led by Council Member Vela.

references.quote: A motion to amend was made by Council Member Vela, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Pool, and approved on a 10-0 vote.
9-1 — Approved

summary: The Mayor will recess the City Council meeting to conduct a Board of Directors' Meeting of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation. (The AHFC agenda is temporarily located at https://www.austintexas.gov/department/city-council/2023/20230309-ahfc.htm) . AIayor Watson reconvened the Council Meeting at 11:49 a.m. DISCUSSION ITEMS CONTINUED 16. Approve a resolution accepting the Equitable Transit-Oriented Development (ETOD) Policy Plan: incorporating ETOD Policy Plan tools for the stations within the boundaries of the Northeast Austin District planning process; initiating amendments to Imagine Austin Comprehensive Plan to adopt elements of the ETOD Policy Plan: and initiating amendments to City Code Title 25. Strategic Outcome(s): Economic Opportunity and Affordability. A motion to approve the resolution was made by Council Alember Qadri and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ellis. The following amendment was made by Council Member Vela and seconded by Council Alember Qadri. The amendment was to add the following Be It Further Resolved clause: "The City Council directs the City Manager to present an implementation plan to clearly identify next steps and identify financing and programmatic support for meeting ETOD goals through implementation of the Policy Toolkit. The implementation plan should include the following: • tools prioritized for implementation; • targeted outcomes for tool implementation; • timeline for tool implementation; • identification of funding sources and other resources for tool implementation; and • performance measures to assess tool implementation success. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED: As part of the implementation plan, the City Council directs the City Manager to do the following: Coordinate with the Austin Transit Partnership, Capital Metro, the City of Austin's Project Connect Office, and the Project Connect Community Advisory Committee to develop population targets for areas around the light rail stations, both individually and as an average along the light rail corridor, with the goal of maximizing the project's score on grant applications in order to maximize federal grant funding competitiveness. • Coordinate with the Austin Transit Partnership, Capital Metro, and the City of Austin's Project Connect Office to evaluate the ETOD Station Area Planning Priorities matrix to prioritize light rail investments and the need for demonstrated outcomes on federal grant applications. • Explore value capture tools such as tax increment financing to fund items such as affordable housing, pedestrian and bicycle improvements, parks, regional water quality facilities, utility relocation, and other necessary infrastructure investments. • Provide scenarios including timelines and staffing needs for developing ETOD station area plans, including scenarios that utilize resources from partnering agencies. • Provide a clear definition and scope of the ETOD overlay to ensure robust affordable housing creation, preservation, and tenant protections in return for relaxed development standards and other programs and incentives. BE IT FITRTHER RESOLVED: The City Council directs the City Manager to provide an update to the Housing and Planning Committee and XIobility Committee no later than May 26th, and to present a full implementation plan to the Housing and Planning Committee and AIobility Committee no later than September 12th. " The following amendment to Council Alember Vela's amendment was made by Council Alember Alison Alter, seconded by Council Member Vela. The amendment was to edit the third bullet point of the second Be It Further Resolved clause to read as follows: "Explore value capture tools such as tax increment financing to incentivize or fund items such as affordable housing, pedestrian and bicycle improvements, parks, regional water quality facilities, utility relocation, and other necessary infrastructure investments. 9, The amendment was included without objection. Council Member Harper-Madison was off the dais. Council Alember Vela's amendment as amended was included without objection. Council Alember Kelly abstained. Council Member Harper-Madison was off the dais. The following amendments were made by Mayor Pro Tem Ellis and seconded by Council Member Vela. The amendment was to edit the Draft ETOD Policy Plan (Attachment A) as follows: On page 29, under Future Station Area Planning Priorities Approach, amend Criteria 2 to read: "Criteria 2: Presence of Publicly Owned Land: Station areas with land owned by the City of Austin and CapMetro should be high priority for planning services because, should it be decided that some of this land is no longer needed for agency operations, these publicly owned sites could be catalysts for increasing ridership and affordable housing. Station areas with land that is owned by another local governmental entity and anticipated to be developed or redeveloped in the next five years should also be high priority for planning services. To determine the station areas containing City and Capl\Ietro owned land, staff used 2021 Travis County Appraisal Data, embedded in the parcel ownership map on the ETOD Interactive Conditions Analysis Dashboard, to calculate the share of City and Caplietro-owned land in each station area and prioritized station areas with larger shares of publicly owned land." On page 36, rename the "Oak Hill" Bus Rapid Transit Station as "Pinnacle," change its Priority for Planning level from Medium to High, and move that line of the table to page 34 to be grouped appropriately. In Appendix E: Station Area Planning Priority Methodology (pages A14 - A23), make conforming changes as appropriate Edit lines 107-109 of the Draft Resolution to read as follows: "WHEREAS, in consideration of the timing of the initial investment in rail under the Project Connect Transit System, rail is first in priority for commencement of all implementation activities, except concurrent commencement may occur for a MetroRapid line that has not yet been awarded federal funding and is assessed to rate uncompetitively for federal funding on the FTA's land use and economic development criteria; " Add the following Whereas clauses between line 133 and 134: "WHEREAS, the City of Austin partners with HousingWorks Austin to annually analyze our success in meeting our Austin Strategic Housing Blueprint goals, and these Scorecards document that we regularly fall short on Goal 1: Affordable Homes in Each District and, within Goal 5, on New Affordable Housing near High- Opportunity Areas; and WHEREAS, MetroRapid Bus lines will dramatically extend the reach of Project Connect's high-capacity transit system into far more neighborhoods than rail will serve alone, including high-opportunity areas where affordable housing could be more easily produced following an ETOD planning process and the application of ETOD development regulations; and" A motion to take up the item at 11:50 a.m. was made by Council Afember Alison Alter, seconded by Council liember Fuentes, and accepted without objection. title: Approve resolution for City shelters operation during extreme weather.
summary: Approve a resolution related to the operation of City shelters during extreme weather events. Council Sponsors: Council Member Mackenzie Kelly, Council Member Ryan Alter, Council Member Zohaib “Zo” Qadri, Mayor Kirk Watson, Council Member José 'Chito' Vela. A motion to approve the resolution was made by Council Member Kelly and seconded by Council Member Velásquez. The following amendment was made by Council Member Ryan Alter, seconded by Council Member Velásquez, and included on an 11-0 vote. 24 “Add the following topic to be considered by the Manager, stakeholders, and subject matter experts in discussions related to extreme weather events and shelter activation: • Opportunities for conducting coordinated assessments for people experiencing homelessness.” The following amendment was made by Council Member Alison Alter, seconded by Council Member Pool, and included on an 11-0 vote. “Insert a new clause at line 8 to read: WHEREAS, on December 13, 2022, the City Council Audit and Finance Committee accepted and discussed the “Emergency Shelters for Dangerous Temperatures Audit,” which included three recommendations related to role clarification and service delivery at cold weather shelters and updates to City operational plans; and Insert a new resolve at line 40 to read: BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED: The City Manager is also directed to continue to implement the recommendations contained in the 2022 “Emergency Shelters for Dangerous Temperatures Audit” and to coordinate that implementation with the other directives contained in this resolution.” The following amendment was made by Council Member Velásquez, seconded by Council Member Alison Alter, and included on an 11-0 vote. “Amend line 46 to read as follows: The City Manager will report back to the Council by June 15, 2023, on (1) recommendations to expand the City’s weather sheltering plan to include all extreme weather events and (2) the feedback and suggestions from the stakeholders and subject matter experts to address activation, registration, transportation and other issues related to the City’s response to sheltering during extreme weather events. (3) recommendations on how best to accommodate on-site and remote shelter registration (4) recommendations on how to implement a waiver of the shelter registration requirement in the case of a State of Disaster declaration from the City or Travis County.” The following amendment was made by Council Member Fuentes, seconded by Council Member Qadri, and included on an 11-0 vote. “Insert a new clause to read: 25 WHEREAS, Council provided direction for improving inclement weather response and shelter in a 2022-2023 budget rider; and Amend the first resolve to read: BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN: The City Manager is also directed to engage and collaborate with stakeholders and subject matter experts, including ECHO’s Inclement Weather Work Group, regarding extreme weather events and shelter activation criteria and processes, including but not limited to the following considerations: • The unique risk factors of vulnerable populations; • The material, logistical and psychological barriers that prevent unhoused residents from having equal access to shelter; • Ways to alleviate any uncertainty within the populations served by extreme weather shelters with registering and staying sheltered, including earlier activation of the shelters; working with community advocates to provide more notice opportunities to the public of shelter activation; evaluating the needs and requirements for registration including, but not limited to accessibility, availability, hours, and locations; expanding access to shelters for families; establishing an extreme weather shelter location in Del Valle; and pausing encampment cleanups at least 48 hours before shelter activation and 48 hours following shelter deactivation; • Engagement with individuals who have lived experience to obtain feedback regarding their stay at extreme weather shelters; • Consideration of partnerships to improve staffing of the shelters and staff training in de-escalation and trauma informed care; and • The lessons learned and the direction provided by the 2022-2023 budget rider for improving inclement weather response and shelter.” The following amendment was made by Council Member Qadri and seconded by Council Member Fuentes. “Amend the first resolve to read: BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN: The City Manager is directed to continue discussions with stakeholders and subject matter experts, including the Cold Weather Shelter Work Group under the ATX Leadership Council and City departments directly engaged with unsheltered individuals, including the Homeless Strategy Division and Austin-Travis County 26 EMS, regarding extreme weather events and shelter activation criteria and processes, including but not limited to the following considerations: • The unique risk factors of vulnerable populations; • The material, logistical and psychological barriers that prevent unhoused residents from having equal access to shelter; • Ways to alleviate any uncertainty within the populations served by extreme weather shelters with registering and staying sheltered, including earlier activation of the shelters, working with community advocates to provide more notice opportunities to the public of shelter activation, expanding registration hours and locations, and pausing encampment cleanups until shelters are deactivated; • Engagement with individuals who have lived experience to obtain feedback regarding their stay at extreme weather shelters; and • Consideration of partnerships to improve staffing of the shelters and staff training in de-escalation and trauma informed care.

references.quote: Amend the second resolve to read: The City Manager will report to the Council by June 15, 2023, on (1) recommendations to expand the City’s weather sheltering plan to include all extreme weather events and (2) the feedback and suggestions from the stakeholders and subject matter experts, in consultation with the ATX Leadership Council for Austin/Travis County Continuum of Care, and in alignment with the written standards for cold weather shelter developed by the Cold Weather Shelter Work Group, to address activation, registration, transportation and other issues related to the City’s response to sheltering during extreme weather events.” The following amendment to Council Member Qadri’s amendment was made by Council Member Kelly and failed for lack of a second.
10-0 — Approved as amended
